summary.title: Callie
summary.pov: Third-person limited (strictly anchored in Callie's sensory experience). The narrative voice mimics her internal cadence: observational, analytical, and physically grounded. No omniscient access to other characters' thoughts unless inferred through action or dialogue.
summary.synopsis: Callie recovers from a wagon pitch injury while monitoring the group's supplies and Duchess's feverish leg condition. The party traverses an endless high plain where Husks drift aimlessly rather than follow lines, forcing Callie to adapt her tracking skills to identify 'pans' (low water traps). She struggles with physical limitations regarding her mother's care but accepts Ines's help. They locate a windmill and tank containing five dead Husks, confirming the danger of pooling ash.
summary.openingState: Callie is lying on her back under the wagon at first light. Physical state: severe pain in left side (two broken ribs), three stitches in scalp, one finger dampness from injury. Mental state: hyper-vigilant, counting breaths and inventory items to ground herself.
turningPoints: Callie realizes she cannot roll onto her injured side; movement is restricted to hands-and-knees or slow rolling on the right.
Pell diagnoses Duchess's leg as 'hotter than last night' but manageable for flat travel only, establishing a strict pace constraint.
The shift in tracking logic: Callie moves from looking for linear tracks (impossible here) to identifying circular pans where Husks pool and die.
Callie attempts to braid her mother's hair; physical pain forces her to yield the task to Ines, marking a moment of vulnerability accepted by both women.
Pell validates Callie's introduction strategy ('I read ground') as superior to pleading for sympathy at their destination.
summary.closingState: Callie is lying on her right side under the wagon in full darkness. Duchess has stopped moving, head up, nostrils wide, shaking quietly near a tank containing five dead Husks. The water cask sloshes with very little remaining.

characters.name: Callie
characters.vocalBehavior: Internal monologue is rhythmic and counting-based (e.g., 'Two ribs... Three stitches'). Dialogue is terse, factual, and devoid of self-pity. She speaks with the authority of a specialist but physical restraint due to pain. Status: High competence, low energy.

characters.name: Pell
characters.vocalBehavior: Measured, deliberate cadence. Uses short declarative sentences. Tone is authoritative but gentle; he speaks with the weight of experience and physical limitation ('slowly, the way a man of sixty-one straightens'). No urgency in his voice despite danger.

characters.name: Callie's Mother
characters.vocalBehavior: Voice is thick and slow. Uses metaphors involving physical objects ('like a glove lies on a table'). She maintains dignity through humor and direct commands, masking pain with stoicism. Status: Confused but lucid; physically failing.

characters.name: Katori
characters.vocalBehavior: Low volume, high pressure. Never raises voice. Uses direct imperatives ('You're riding'). Tone is pragmatic and unsentimental but protective. She cuts through Callie's self-pity with cold logic.

characters.name: Ines
characters.vocalBehavior: Minimalist speech. Precise, exact movements mirrored in her voice (e.g., 'Without any part left over'). Calm and efficient.

locations: The high plain (vast, flat, grey slabs of concrete road, no trees, sky coming down like a bowl)
A shallow pan/dip in the grass (water trap for Husks)
terms: Husk: A creature that drifts aimlessly on flat ground until it pools in low spots.
The Edge: The specific skill of reading terrain to predict movement (to be taught later).
Handful: Unit of measurement for ash/supplies.
Barrow/Wagon: Interchangeable terms used by the mother due to confusion; refers to their transport.
summary.actionCadence: Slow, laborious physical movements contrasted with sharp visual scanning. The rhythm is dictated by Duchess's gait (slow, dipping) and Callie's breathing (counting). Dialogue pauses are frequent, allowing for observation of the landscape.
summary.emotionalRegister: Restrained endurance. Pain is acknowledged as a fact to be managed, not dramatized. There is no panic regarding the Husks; only tactical assessment. A moment of shared tenderness between Callie and her mother (holding hands) breaks the stoicism but remains brief.
narrationRisks: The opening counting sequence ('Two ribs... Three stitches') must not be rushed or flattened into a list; it requires a rhythmic, breath-synced delivery to convey pain management.

Callie's internal realization about the 'no grade' and drifting Husks is complex logic. The narrator must slow down here to let the audience follow the deduction from linear tracking to pooling behavior without losing tension.

The mother's dialogue ('It was a barrow when I got hold of it...') requires a specific vocal texture: thick, slightly disjointed, but clear enough for Callie (and listener) to understand her confusion about reality shifting.
carryForward: Callie is physically compromised and must ride on the board; she cannot walk far.
Duchess's leg condition has stabilized slightly but requires strict flat-ground travel only.
The group knows they are approaching a water source (the tank) which contains dead Husks, implying immediate danger or resource scarcity.
Callie is mentally preparing her introduction to the gate ('I read ground') and has one line ready.
